name: Chinese face-slimming roller (Yoni-style jade roller)

card.summary: A handheld stone roller rolled over the face to massage, depuff and give a temporary slimmer, fresher look.
card.note: Effects are temporary; keep the roller clean to avoid transferring bacteria to skin.

quick.overview:
A jade roller is a small handheld tool with a stone barrel, often jade or quartz, on one or both ends of a handle. It is rolled over the face and neck, and users say it temporarily reduces morning puffiness and makes the face look slimmer.

It descends from traditional Chinese facial massage and gua sha, and rose in popularity through social media. A 2023 review in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology looked at gua sha, jade rollers and facial massage within dermatology.
quick.how: Users roll the tool across cleansed skin, usually upward and outward from the centre of the face, often after applying serum or oil, and some keep it in the fridge for a cooling effect. Sessions last a few minutes and are repeated daily or on a regular schedule.
quick.risks: Rolling is gentle and mostly causes temporary redness. Shared or unwashed rollers can carry bacteria, and rolling over active acne or broken skin can irritate it. Stone quality varies between products.

lead: The jade roller, sometimes marketed as a Chinese face-slimming or Yoni-style roller, is a facial massage tool with one or two stone rollers. Users run it across the skin to massage, cool and visually smooth the face. [1]

Brands and users describe lymphatic drainage, depuffing and a slimmer face contour as the aims, with the stone's coolness helping reduce puffiness. The practice is linked to gua sha, a traditional Chinese technique that uses stone tools, whose facial form surged on TikTok in 2021 to 2022. [1][2]
Chinese utility-model patents from 2005 and 2008 describe jade-roller beauty devices with warming mechanisms, showing the tool's use in cosmetic devices. [3][4]

chain: Stone roller glides over face and neck
Massage and coolness move fluid and calm puffiness
angle.text: Users roll it over the face in the morning to reduce puffiness and sharpen the look of the jaw and cheeks. The effect described is short-lived and similar to what a cool compress or massage provides.

paras: Most rollers have a larger stone for cheeks and forehead and a smaller one for eyes and nose. Some use quartz or other stones; devices with warming elements have been patented in China. [3][4]

Wikipedia traces gua sha to China, with formal use in traditional Chinese medicine from the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644). Stone tools including jade are used, and facial gua sha became widely shared on TikTok in 2021 to 2022 for lymphatic drainage and skin rejuvenation. [2]

The 2023 Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology review asked whether gua sha, jade rollers and facial massage have benefits within dermatology. [1] Wikipedia describes gua sha as lacking high-quality evidence of clinical benefit, and notes risks such as bruising, with infection a concern when tools are unsterilised or skin is broken. [2]
No studies found specific to jade rollers beyond a 2023 narrative review of facial massage tools in dermatology. [1]
